item.title: Podcast: The Orioles and their non-slugging outfielders
item.description: BALTIMORE, MARYLAND - SEPTEMBER 23: Colton Cowser #17 of the Baltimore Orioles walks back to the dugout out during game one of a baseball doubleheader against the Toronto Blue Jays at Oriole Park at Camden Yards on September 23, 2026 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Mitchell Layton/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Orioles had a bottom 10 outfield by public defensive metrics. Even worse, they had the lowest slugging percentage of all 30 MLB teams for their outfielders. Mike Elias’s plan of getting power out of his outfield with his free agent signing Tyler O’Neill, his trade acquisition Taylor Ward, and his draft picks Colton Cowser and Dylan Beavers, was a total bust. Between injuries and poor performances, there was a rotating cast of players, some of whom were just… so bad. In contrast to last week’s episode, where the Orioles relievers were better than expected, this outfield group was just so much worse than expected. Anybody could have guessed there were going to be defensive liabilities from the group going into the season. Even so, the magnitude was so much greater, and they sure didn’t get the power trade-off that Elias was probably imagining. item.title: Anthony Joshua must avoid this exact Fabio Wardley mistake to topple Tyson Fury
item.description: As “Triple D” Daniel “Dynamite” Dubois dismantled Fabio Wardley under the dome of the O2 on Saturday, there was double deja vu . And yes, fine, the alliteration there is about as excessive as the punishment Wardley that absorbed . Five months on from the first loss of his career, Wardley was stopped by Dubois again. That was the first familiarity, but the second is altogether more intriguing. We’ll get to that soon. Firstly though, the damage admittedly looked different this time , as did the pattern of the fight. May’s heavyweight clash in Manchester saw Wardley drop Dubois in the first 10 seconds and again in round three, before Dubois rallied, took over the fight, and stopped a bloody Wardley late on. On Saturday, the fate of the WBO title was decided inside two rounds, although there’s an argument that it was really decided in the opening 20 seconds ; that was when a jackhammer right cross hurt Wardley, who never truly recovered. Daniel Dubois (left) stopped Fabio Wardley inside two rounds in their rematch (Getty) The second case of deja vu , though, will have flitted through fans during the five minutes in which Wardley tried to jolt himself awake from this nightmare. More than once, Wardley tried to deter Dubois with a rear uppercut, and more than once he was punished for it. It was the same shot that cost Anthony Joshua in his beating by Dubois in 2024, when Ben Davison was in his corner – just as he was in Wardley’s on Saturday. That punch can feel an unwise choice at the best of times, a technique that leaves you vulnerable, but these were the worst of times. Davison might bring Joshua that confidence, but there is a fine line between confidence and a dangerous commitment to the wrong tactic. Against Fury, Davison and Joshua must be switched on like never before.

item.title: Giants rave about ‘natural-born leader’ J.J. McCarthy, as John Harbaugh considers QB change
item.description: It was just a small sample size, but J.J. McCarthy played quite well Sunday. So will he start next week in Houston, with Jameis Winston heading to the bench? That remains unclear. For now, Giants coach John Harbaugh is at least keeping the door open for a starting quarterback change. But if McCarthy does take over for Winston as Jaxson Dart’s replacement, his teammates are plenty confident in him, based on what he showed late in Sunday’s 34-27 loss to the Saints. “J.J. is a natural leader,” running back Tyrone Tracy said. “What he acted like in the huddle, that’s what he acts like every single day in practice. That’s how he commands the huddle. He’s a natural-born leader. He brought us back. At the same time, we already knew what to expect from J.J.” Rookie wide receiver Malachi Fields felt equally impressed by McCarthy’s demeanor in the huddle during Sunday’s fourth quarter. “Just composed,” Fields told NJ.com. “Just a leader. He goes and executes.” If the Giants start McCarthy next week, does Sunday’s performance inspire confidence in him? “Definitely, just showing what he’s capable of,” Fields said. “And showing that he’s willing to do it – and taking command like that. So, yeah.” The Giants trailed 34-10 when McCarthy replaced Winston with 11:25 left in the game. Then McCarthy led a furious comeback. He had a fourth-down throw from the Saints’ 14-yard line with 12 seconds left — a chance to stunningly force overtime. But McCarthy’s pass for Isaiah Likely sailed incomplete. Yes, McCarthy’s numbers benefited from the Saints’ prevent defense. Yes, the Saints’ defense is not very good overall. And yes, the Texans present much bigger challenges. They are seventh in Pro Football Focus’ pass rush ratings, so they make a habit of tormenting quarterbacks, especially inexperienced ones like McCarthy. Still, McCarthy can take lots of confidence from what he accomplished Sunday, when he put together a crazy fourth-quarter stat line: 11-of-21 passing, 243 yards, one touchdown, one interception and a 90.0 passer rating. McCarthy’s 243 yards were the second-most passing yards by a replacement quarterback in the fourth quarter over the past 25 seasons. He also showcased his speed on Sunday with a 28-yard scramble. item.title: How to Watch Illinois vs. Baylor Exhibition: Game Time, TV Channel, Online Streaming and Odds
item.description: CINCINNATI, OHIO - OCTOBER 17: Stefan Vaaks #7 of the Illinois Fighting Illini holds the ball while being guarded by Myles Colvin #6 of the Cincinnati Bearcats in the second half during an exhibition game at Fifth Third Arena on October 17, 2026 in Cincinnati, Ohio. (Photo by Dylan Buell/Getty Images) | Getty Images How to Watch Illinois vs. Baylor (Exhibition) Game Time: 7 p.m. Friday TV Channel: N/A Online Streaming: B1G+ Odds: N/A Quick Hits: Illinois Fighting Illini (0-0, 0-0 Big Ten) Head Coach: Brad Underwood (10th season) 2025-26: 28-9 (15-5 Big Ten); lost in Final Four to UCONN Last Game: Illinois 105, Cincinnati 96 (Exhibition) Baylor Bears (0-0, 0-0 Big 12) Head coach: Scott Drew (23rd season) 2025-26: 17-17 (6-12 Big 12) What Happened the Last Time These Two Teams Played? Illinois leads the all-time series 3-1. Dec. 2, 2020: Baylor 82, Illinois 69 For 30 minutes, the Illini proved they belong with the big boys of college basketball. Despite hanging with the Bears for a majority of the game, No. 2 Baylor (3-0) pulled away from No. 5 Illinois (3-1) 82-69 in the Jimmy V Classic in Indianapolis on Wednesday. “It was a dog fight for a good portion of the game,” said head coach Brad Underwood after the Illini took their first lost of the year. “I give a lot of credit to Baylor. There’s a reason they won 23 straight. They showed their tenacity, their toughness.” When you find yourself going up against one of the best defensive teams in the nation, you’re going to need somebody outside of the usual suspects to step up. With Ayo Dosunmu getting locked up for the majority of the game, the Illini needed production from somewhere else. Giorgi Bezhanishvili was the guy. The junior gave Illinois 15 points and four rebounds off the bench — 13 of those points in the first half. Kofi Cockburn missed a hefty chunk of time in the first half with two fouls — and picked up his third less than a minute into the second half — so the Illini needed the Rustavi, Georgia, native to eat some minutes. “I think we are right there,” Bezhanishvili said after the loss. “We just have to clean up little mistakes. Trent (Frazier) isn’t going to have nights like that with 6 turnovers. Kofi (Cockburn) isn’t going to have nights like that. (Ayo Dosunmu) isn’t going to shoot like that.” “I’m really excited about moving forward with Giorgi,” Underwood said. Free throws hurt, as the Illini converted just one time in their first six attempts from the charity stripe. The game also started sloppy for both teams, understandable for two offenses that only had a few tune-ups before taking on one of the nation’s top defenses. Difference is, it stayed sloppy for Illinois.

item.description: Spurs keen on move for €30m Brazilian stopper Tottenham transfer news: Otavio pursuit faces €30m test as Cruzeiro hold firm Tottenham’s reported interest in Otavio presents a familiar recruitment dilemma: move early for a promising player or wait for further evidence and risk facing greater competition. The Cruzeiro goalkeeper has attracted attention after establishing himself in the first team, with Spurs among the clubs said to be following his progress. At 20, he offers the prospect of development alongside the experience he is already gaining in demanding fixtures. The financial terms could determine whether that interest goes any further. Cruzeiro are reportedly seeking an initial fee of between €25 million and €30 million, while a contract running until 2031 gives them considerable control over his future. IMAGO Otavio emerges on Tottenham’s transfer radar According to Fussball News, in a report covered by CaughtOffside, Tottenham are monitoring Otavio as they assess their goalkeeping options. His opportunity at Cruzeiro came following an injury to the experienced Cassio. Otavio took advantage, becoming a regular and attracting attention through performances in the Copa Libertadores and prominent domestic matches. The qualities highlighted in the reporting include his reflexes, composure and distribution. Together, those attributes explain why clubs looking beyond their immediate requirements might consider him an appealing prospect. For Tottenham, the potential attraction is clear. item.title: Morgan Gibbs-White fined after his car ran red light
item.description: Nottingham Forest's Morgan Gibbs-White failed to respond to two police letters, according to court documents [Reuters] England and Nottingham Forest attacking midfielder Morgan Gibbs-White has been handed a £1,000 court bill after his Range Rover was caught running a red light. The 26-year-old's vehicle was caught on camera going past a set of lights in West Bridgford, Nottinghamshire, 1.1 seconds after they turned red. Gibbs-White, who earned his first England cap in 2024, failed to respond to two police letters asking him to confirm if he had been driving at the time of the red light offence, according to court documents. Last Tuesday, he was convicted by a court of failing to provide the identity of a driver at the time of an offence. Nottinghamshire Police put out an alert on Gibbs-White's car when the force tried to investigate the traffic light incident, and found the number plate registered with the DVLA was one letter different from what was on the vehicle. Staffordshire Police then pulled over the Range Rover in April and confirmed it belonged to Gibbs-White. At Southern Derbyshire Magistrates' Court, he was fined £660, given six penalty points on his licence and ordered to pay £120 in costs and a £264 victim surcharge. Gibbs-White was called up to Thomas Tuchel's recent England squad for the Nations League [Press Association] A court official said Gibbs-White did not enter a plea or mitigation, and was sentenced behind closed doors under the fast-track Single Justice Procedure. Court papers show a Nottinghamshire Police camera caught Gibbs-White's car going past a red traffic light at 15:17 GMT on 28 January in Radcliffe Road. "At the time of the offence, the vehicle was captured failing to comply with a red light signal, the time into the red light was recorded as 1.1 seconds," a police worker wrote in her statement. Gibbs-White was banned from driving for six months in May last year after he was caught speeding six times in the space of three months. At the time, he was ordered to pay just under £4,000 in fines for the spate of offences, including two speeding tickets acquired on the same day. Gibbs-White, who signed for Forest in 2022 from Wolverhampton Wanderers, has made 10 appearances for England and was called up to Thomas Tuchel's recent squad for the Nations League. item.title: Henderson happy Chelsea ‘in right direction’ after beating Everton
item.description: FILE PHOTO - Chelsea's Jordan Henderson celebrates after the English Premier League soccer match between Chelsea and Bournemouth at Stamford Bridge. (is associated with: «Henderson happy Chelsea ‘in right direction’ after beating Everton») Adam Davy/PA Wire/dpa Jordan Henderson believes Chelsea are “going in the right direction” after Xabi Alonso’s new-look side moved up to fourth in the Premier League. The Blues signed off for the international break with an alarming 3-0 defeat by Brentford but they have bounced back by securing successive victories against Bournemouth and Everton. Henderson, 36, scored a brace in the 5-1 win against Bournemouth before completing another 90 minutes in as many matches in Chelsea’s 2-0 win at Everton. And he said: “I’m loving playing football at the minute. “I’ve come back in the last month or so from my injury and it’s an absolute privilege and honour to be playing with some of the players in this team. “I’m just enjoying it, working with them every day and playing with them out on the pitch. There’s some top quality, top talent here, and I really feel like the team’s beginning to take shape in terms of the togetherness and everything. “There’s been a lot of new change in the summer – new coaching staff and players coming in – but I really feel that the togetherness is coming, not only in training during the week on the field, off the field as well. That’s going to be important for us going forward and I’m loving every second of it. “I know we’ve still got a lot to improve on as a team, but I feel as though in the last couple of weeks we’re going in the right direction. So, we’ll go back to the training ground and keep working hard for the next game.” Chelsea host Tottenham at Stamford Bridge on Saturday before travelling to Liverpool in the fourth round of the League Cup. They will be without goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez after he suffered a fractured jaw in Chelsea’s win at the Hill Dickinson Stadium. The Argentina international said he will be “back in a few weeks”.

item.title: Guehi insists players have 'trust and belief' in Man City after charges
item.description: Manchester City defender Marc Guehi speaks during a press conference on the eve of the club's Champions League tie at home to AEK Athens (Darren Staples) Manchester City defender Marc Guehi said on Monday a "pretty calm" squad have "a lot of trust and belief in the football club" despite the English giants being found guilty of more than 100 breaches of Premier League financial rules. City have made an impressive start to the season under new manager Enzo Maresca, winning all of their seven opening league games to lead the Premier League table by three points from champions Arsenal. But those results have been achieved against the backdrop of a mass of guilty verdicts, which have led to calls for City to be hit with huge points deductions, colossal fines and even the stripping of some of their Premier League titles. Significantly, however, no punishments have yet been announced and City, who have repeatedly denied wrongdoing, are appealing against the verdicts. The only blemish to City's on field form so far in the current campaign has been a 4-2 defeat in the Champions League by title-holders Paris Saint-Germain, with City eager to returning to winning ways in Europe at home to AEK Athens on Tuesday. England defender Guehi, speaking at a pre-match press conference, said: "The team spirit has been really good, every single person, player, staff and fans are backing us and it has been great to see. "We're pretty calm. There's a lot of relaxed faces because we have a lot of trust and belief in the football club and what's been going on here." "It can be very easy to be affected by the noise that's going on. But I'm so happy to see the team spirit, the team bonding and everyone taking to what's happening and just focusing on the football," he added. Under collaborative replay, a command center official confirms the booth’s decision to clear “scores and turnovers.” The end-of-game clock is not on that list. What is missing is a required, independent read of the clock before the referee declares the game over. The NFL is not a model either. Since 2016, the game clock has been reviewable . But at the end of a half, a timing error counts only when “more than one second should be put on the clock.” Even the NFL could let a 0:01 miss stand. The time-out is led by a named person and documented in the chart. Anyone in the room, including the newest nurse, can stop the line. When something goes wrong, the error is reported and presented at morbidity and mortality conference, where surgeons review their own complications before peers. College football generates billions. In a twist Michigan fans will appreciate, the University of Michigan Health System moved from “deny and defend” to full disclosure, and a 2010 study found that claims, lawsuits and liability costs all fell. Honesty built trust. Notre Dame fans will get over this one as long as they beat Miami... item.title: Matthäus backs in-form Niclas Füllkrug for Germany return
item.description: Matthäus backs in-form Niclas Füllkrug for Germany return After struggling for form at West Ham United and during his loan spell at AC Milan, Niclas Füllkrug has impressed since returning to Werder Bremen last summer. Having scored a brace against Paderborn at the weekend, the 33-year-old West Ham loanee now sits joint-top of the Bundesliga scoring charts with six goals, alongside Bayer Leverkusen's Patrik Schick. According to Germany legend Lothar Matthäus, it's therefore only natural that Füllkrug is once again being discussed as a potential option for the German national team. “Füllkrug feels comfortable in Bremen, and it shows. At West Ham and Milan, he did not feel the warmth, affection and trust that he receives at Werder,” Matthäus wrote in a column for Sky Germany. At 33, Matthäus believes the forward could add valuable experience to Jürgen Klopp's young Germany squad. “The numbers speak for him, even if he is getting on in years. Jürgen Klopp wants to rejuvenate the national team, but the younger players are still too inconsistent in their performances,” Matthäus continued. “Having an experienced option like Füllkrug coming off the bench would give me confidence. However, the final decision rests with the national team coach.” Füllkrug has scored 14 goals in 24 appearances for Germany. His last international outing came in June 2025. Germany will play their next game against Serbia in the UEFA Nations League on November 13.

item.title: Newcastle board reach definitive decision on Matthias Jaissle’s future after sluggish Premier League start
item.description: Newcastle United v Aston Villa FC - Premier League 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Board stand firm behind Jaissle Jaissle is under no immediate pressure at Newcastle despite a disappointing opening to the campaign. The club hierarchy is prepared to give the 38-year-old manager time to establish his methods and turn results around, as per TEAMtalk . The Magpies currently sit 11th in the Premier League table with just eight points from their opening seven fixtures. A weekend 1-0 defeat to Aston Villa followed a heavy 4-1 loss away to newly promoted Coventry , fueling frustration among the fan base. Some supporters have grown restless over the early form, with one influential fanzine even calling for the manager to be sacked. However, senior figures at St James' Park retain firm belief in the project Jaissle is constructing. Rebuilding after major summer exits Rebuilding after major summer exits The Newcastle board fully anticipated a turbulent transitional phase after losing three key figures in the summer transfer window. Sandro Tonali , Anthony Gordon , and Bruno Guimaraes all departed the club in a single window. Stripping the squad of its midfield core and a primary attacking threat meant fluctuating results were always expected. According to the same report, hierarchy figures view the recent struggles as an inevitable consequence of those squad changes rather than a flaw in the manager's tactical system. Furthermore, the report also describe Jaissle's training sessions as brilliant, praising his focus on high-intensity pressing and structured build-up play. The hierarchy remains convinced that these methods will pay off over the long term. Squad remains firmly behind manager Inside the dressing room, the mood among the players remains overwhelmingly positive despite the disappointing run of results. The squad enjoys working under the former Red Bull Salzburg and Al-Ahli coach and values the clarity of his tactical instructions. Players believe that early-season difficulties are only temporary as new tactical combinations begin to click. They expect performances to improve significantly once team chemistry settles and key absences are managed effectively. Rather than panicking, the hierarchy views the current situation as a necessary phase in reshaping the team around younger and newly arrived players. The current form has not triggered any serious boardroom concern. Time and trust at St James' Park Time and trust at St James' Park Jaissle retains both the public and private support of the Newcastle leadership as he implements his philosophy. The manager will now focus on restoring momentum and guiding his side back up the Premier League table. The Magpies are now preparing to face Crystal Palace at Selhurst Park on Sunday, followed by a clash against Everton in the Carabao Cup next week.

item.description: [Getty Images] Leicester City attacking midfielder Kamari Doyle said the team "can't hold off" now in their desire to improve their stuttering start to the season. item.description: Napoli confirm Alisson Santos blow on first appearance after recovering from injury Napoli have confirmed that Alisson Santos suffered a medium-grade hamstring injury at the end of Saturday’s 1-0 defeat against Venezia, which was the Brazilian’s first game back after recovering from the exact same issue. Napoli confirm Alisson Santos has suffered the same hamstring injury again Napoli have confirmed in a statement on the club website that the 24-year-old attacker reported for medical tests on Monday after picking up an injury towards the end of Sunday’s shock 1-0 defeat against Venezia, who had not picked up a single point in Serie A before this weekend. The club has confirmed that Alisson has suffered a medium-grade hamstring injury, the exact same injury he suffered during a 1-0 Champions League defeat against Arsenal back in September. item.title: “Source of immense pride and honour”: Amad reacts to incredible Man United career milestone
item.description: “Source of immense pride and honour”: Amad reacts to incredible Man United career milestone Manchester United forward Amad Diallo has sent a message after reaching a significant milestone for the club. Landmark achievement Amad made his 100th appearance for United during Sunday’s 1-1 draw with Leeds United at Elland Road. Before the contest, he spoke to club media and reflected on his time so far at the club, as well as what he hopes to achieve in the coming years. The Ivorian made his return to action during the 1-1 draw with Tottenham Hotspur and was once again included in the starting XI that was held by Leeds . He was on the pitch for 90 minutes vs. Leeds, primarily playing as a right wing-back as Michael Carrick resorted to a back five. In making 100 appearances, Amad becomes the 230th player to reach a century of appearances for United and just the fourth from Africa after Eric Bailly, Quinton Fortune and Andre Onana. He made his debut against Real Sociedad on 18 February 2021. Amad has plundered 16 goals for the Red Devils. The 24-year-old took to social media after the draw with Daniel Farke’s men and delivered a heartfelt message. Amad’s reaction He wrote on Instagram, “100 matches in a Manchester United shirt. A source of immense pride and an honour I will never take for granted.” “Thank you to my teammates, the staff, and the fans who have been with me on this journey.” “Wearing this shirt means representing a rich history and giving my absolute best in every single match.” “But my ambition doesn’t stop at a number of appearances: I want to win trophies with this club. Together with my teammates, I want us to build something we can be proud of—and to give our fans the emotions they truly deserve.” View this post on Instagram A post shared by Amad Diallo (@amaddiallo19) Amad and his teammates are next in action on Wednesday when they face Como in the Champions League. item.description: Salman Ali Agha made a significant addition to Pakistan’s ODI record books with a century against Sri Lanka in the opening match of the ongoing tri-series, becoming the country’s most prolific centurion among batters who have regularly featured at No. 5 or lower. The former Pakistan T20I captain struck 107 off 90 balls, including 10 fours and a six, to help the hosts post 305 in 49.5 overs at the Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium on Sunday. Pakistan went on to register a 37-run victory after Sri Lanka suffered a dramatic collapse late in their chase. The hundred was Agha’s fourth in 54 ODIs for Pakistan, with all four coming while batting at No. 5 or lower. His latest effort took him past former Pakistan batter Mohammad Yousuf, with whom he had previously shared the national record for the most ODI centuries from those positions. Yousuf scored three hundreds while batting at No. 5 or lower in ODIs. Between 1998 and 2009, he played 114 matches in those positions, establishing himself as one of Pakistan’s most accomplished batters. Agha has now moved ahead of him, with three of his four ODI centuries coming specifically at No. 5. He has achieved that feat in just 33 matches batting in the position, making him the first Pakistani to score three ODI hundreds at No. 5. Before Agha, Yousuf was the only Pakistan batter to have scored multiple ODI centuries at that position, registering two hundreds in 84 matches at No. 5. While Agha has established a new Pakistan record, the overall mark for the most ODI centuries scored at No. 5 or lower remains with England’s Jos Buttler and South Africa’s David Miller. item.title: Wales great Evans to leave role as Lions chair
item.description: Ieuan Evans played club rugby for Llanelli and Bath [Getty Images] Ieuan Evans will stand down as chair of the British and Irish Lions on Wednesday after almost four years in the role. The former Wales captain, who played on tours to Australia in 1989, New Zealand in 1993 and South Africa in 1997, was appointed in 2022 and is coming to the end of his term. Ex-wing Evans was tour manager last year when the men's team recorded a series victory against the Wallabies under Andy Farrell. The Lions have started the search for a new chair before next year's inaugural women's tour to New Zealand. "I am incredibly proud of what has been achieved over the past four years, particularly the success of the 2025 tour, the progress made towards the first Lions Women's tour and the strength of the organisation as it looks ahead to an exciting new chapter," said Evans. Northampton 'security incident' believed to be a hoax The players that staked late claims for Wales spots The 62-year-old, who scored the Lions' pivotal series-winning try in the third Test against Australia in 1989, oversaw governance changes with the recruitment of independent directors to the board. Lions chief executive Ben Calveley said: "His infectious passion for the Lions and understanding of what makes this organisation so special has been evident throughout his time in the role."

item.title: ‘I want to be part of the future success’ – Guehi says Man City players ‘calm’ over financial charges verdict
item.description: ‘I want to be part of the future success’ – Guehi says Man City players ‘calm’ over financial charges verdict Marc Guehi says Manchester City’s players have remained calm and united after the club were found guilty of breaching Premier League financial rules. The defender revealed the squad were informed immediately of the findings from the independent commission, and says there has been no panic inside the group, with the club still appealing the verdict . “The club notified everyone straight away so we were pretty calm,” Guehi said. “There were a lot of relaxed faces because we have a lot of trust and belief in the club and what’s been going on here.” Guehi believes the situation has actually highlighted the togetherness within the squad. “It’s been nice, it’s been good,” he said. “We get to see a lot of togetherness. The team spirit has been really fantastic from every single person and player – especially the staff and the fans that are backing us. “To be honest, it’s been great to see.” The England international also stressed the importance of ignoring outside noise and concentrating on football. “It can be very easy to listen to the noise and be affected by everything going on but I’m so happy to see the team spirit and everyone taking to what’s happening and just focusing on the football.” Guehi also spoke warmly about his own experience at City and his desire to be part of the club’s future. “Ever since I’ve got here they’ve been nothing but fantastic with me,” he said. “The support that I’ve had with tough times on and off the pitch. “I’m aware of the success the club has had and I want to be part of the future success. “You get the sense from everyone at the football club that it’s a family club, people love one another. “I can only talk from my experience.” Stay up to date with all the latest Manchester City news by joining our Man City WhatsApp channel .

item.title: Pellegrini speaks ahead of Roma’s clash with Slovan: “My priority was to stay here and I’m happy it happened.”
item.description: Pellegrini speaks ahead of Roma’s clash with Slovan: “My priority was to stay here and I’m happy it happened.” Lorenzo Pellegrini could also be among the key players in the match against Slovan Bratislava. Roma’s number 7, after coming on as a substitute in the league match against Genoa, is a candidate for a starting spot against the Slovakian club in the Champions League. Speaking at a press conference from Trigoria, the Roma midfielder spoke about tomorrow’s match. “I’m very well, very calm mentally, we’re working physically. Obviously, the fact of, as you said, not being on the pitch for so long required, let’s say, especially initially, a reintegration, in short, giving this reintegration the right amount of time. Obviously I missed it, I miss it, but I can definitely still raise my physical level.” “Initially it was definitely more difficult, I wasn’t at the level of my teammates who worked harder than me, but we’re continuing to work and I’m very happy, I’m very calm. We’re working well, this is an exceptional group, where during the week we’re strong, where on Sundays we’re stronger than during the week because we have to win games. So we’re fine, I’m fine. The one-year renewal was a decision that, in short, we made, that the club made and that I accepted. Simply this.” “The renewal? We always stayed in touch with the coach, with the staff, to, in short, continue, to try to continue this journey together, which in the end is what happened.” “As I said before, at that point, it was important for me to be healthy, first and foremost. (Photo by Jaiden Tripi/Getty Images) | Getty Images There are genuinely positive signs about the direction of the New York Jets franchise. The 2026 New York Jets are a bad football team. I would argue that both of those statements are true, and this team’s 26-19 loss to the Patriots in Week 6 proves it. This season is not only about wins and losses for the Jets. That statement has been uttered so often that it’s practically a cliche, but there is truth to it. Wins and losses aren’t irrelevant for this team, but there are major implications for this team’s future that go beyond where the Jets finish in the standings this season. The most important is the success of the rookie class from the 2026 NFL Draft. The success or failure of a rebuild largely depends on Draft classes being successful. It’s too early to make definitive statements, but we have seen positive signs from all three picks this team made in this year’s first round. They look like they belong. We can’t declare anybody a star yet, and the class has shown some degree of inconsistency. Still, none has looked overmatched on an NFL field. More than that, we have seen a monster Kenyon Sadiq game and a monster David Bailey game. Now we have a monster Omar Cooper game. The rookie, playing the first full game of his career, had 6 catches for 103 yards and a touchdown and had a second touchdown taken off the board on a suspect penalty call in the first quarter. Bad teams come in all shapes and sizes in this league. The 2024 Jets were a team full of overpaid big name players who were past their prime, had massive egos, and didn’t play together. The 2025 Jets were a team that was just completely overmatched from a talent perspective most weeks. The 2026 Jets don’t resemble either of those squads. There aren’t many big names on this roster, and they no longer look incapable of competing. Still, while the talent level has improved, this is still a team with a below average base of it. In a league with a salary cap of $301.2 million, the 2026 Jets have an astounding $116.6 million in dead money. Yes, the Jets are being charged over 38 percent of the Jets’ salary cap dollars to players who are no longer with the team. They don’t tell you about that in the fine print when you decided to go “all in” around a 40 year old quarterback. Despite their improvements, the Jets remain the less talented team most weeks when they take the field. They have to be due to their cap situation. There was no way to build a top notch football team in 2026. Teams like the Jets can still win games, but they have a lower margin for error. They need to play smart and opportunistic football. They can’t afford to overcome errors. Much of that comes back to coaching. It’s difficult to say where the responsibility for players ends and where it begins for coaching when we discuss a team’s success or failure. When it comes to evaluating coaching, I ask myself a simple question. Are the coaches making this team more likely or less likely to have success? One test I have is whether you see a team understand how to play situational football. When you’re in a two minute drill or at the end of a quarter, things are moving too quickly for there to be instruction from the sideline. Either the coaching staff has drilled into players what must be done and what cannot be done or it hasn’t. The Jets were outscored 10-0 in the final two minutes of the first half in this loss, which led Zack Rosenblatt of The Athletic to dig up a truly incredible stat. The Jets have been outscored 100-6 in the final two minutes in the second quarter since Aaron Glenn was hired, according to TruMedia. Have seen a few figures out there but that seems to be the accurate one. That’s zero TDs and two FGs for the Jets with 11 TDs and eight FGs… — Zack Rosenblatt (@ZackBlatt) October 19, 2026 Keep in mind that these scenarios take up only two minutes of each game. That stat has been accumulated over 46 minutes of game time, just a little over three quarters of football. I don’t even know how it’s possible to get outscored 100-6 in 46 minutes of NFL action under any circumstances. But we have seen firsthand the lack of situational football training from the Jets at the end of the half in four of six games. Three times the clock has expired on the offense driving with the ball. In yesterday’s game, a quick three and out that lasted only 23 seconds gave the Patriots the ball back with a chance to get another score before halftime. In those situations, the smartest teams in the league strike a good balance between trying to score and running out the clock to prevent the other team from having enough time to score in the event of a punt. In yesterday’s game, the Jets didn’t even run the ball once. The Patriots were only forced to use a single timeout on the drive. They ended up scoring a touchdown with 14 seconds left on the clock and no timeouts. I understand that you need to throw more than you run in a two minute drill, but it’s standard practice to run the ball once to melt the clock as a hedge against the other team having too much time if the event of a quick three and out. What made this more confounding is the Jets spent the bulk of the first half showing an unwillingness to do anything other than run the ball. Three of the first four Jets drives on offense stalled when Frank Reich called four consecutive runs, and the fourth run netted either 1 or 0 yards. It’s always easy to get on playcalling when it doesn’t work, but an essential part of play calling means staying ahead of the defense. When an offense keeps stalling because it won’t stop running and is eventually stopped, it’s pretty clear there’s a degree of stubborness at play that is hurting the offense. I could go on about the coaching. There is plenty to discuss. We could talk about players not being aware of an obvious hard count situation as the clock is expiring at the end of the quarter or some shaky calls on the other side of the ball. The bottom line is that the Jets show many signs of a poorly coached football team. While their talent level is better than in the past, they aren’t yet good enough to bad execution and poor situational coaching. Few Jets fans are going to leave that game feeling very happy. It was an ugly loss. When it comes to the overall trajectory of the 2026 season, though, it’s perfectly fine to feel a tad conflicted. The Jets are showing some real positives, namely this rookie class. For the first time in four years, it looks like this team is on the verge of hitting a Draft class in a big way. Still, much work remains. This team is losing more than it’s winning. And its coaching is part of that story.

item.description: LAS VEGAS, NV - OCTOBER 18: Keon Coleman #0 of the Buffalo Bills celebrates after scoring a touchdown against the Las Vegas Raiders during the second half of an NFL football game at Allegiant Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Buffalo Bills (5-1) will head into their bye week sitting atop the AFC East and holding the No. 2 seed in the conference following a 33-30 road win over the Las Vegas Raiders Sunday afternoon. Today’s edition of Buffalo Rumblinks recaps the good, the bad, and the ugly from Buffalo’s 33-30 win over the Raiders. Check out the assessments below and then let us know why you’re optimistic about this Bills team and what concerns you the most in the comments section. Bills hang on for another shootout win vs. Raiders Josh Allen came through with another clutch, turnover-free effort to help the Bills escape Sin City with a win over the Raiders. Allen completed 23 of 33 passes for 255 yards with two touchdowns—including an insane escape attempt that culminated in a flip throw TD to Keon Coleman—with zero interceptions as the Bills head into their bye week with the top scoring offense in the NFL (32.83 points/game). But Buffalo’s offense really found its groove when James Cook III was heavily involved. Cook averaged nearly five yards per rush in finishing with 22 carries for 95 yards and a TD, plus three catches for 58 yards, and he didn’t fumble the ball once after two fumbles in the win vs. the Los Angeles Rams. After the Raiders pulled even in the fourth quarter, Allen found Cook for a 26-yard pass that set up Cook’s rushing TD that gave the Bills the lead for good. Speaking of Coleman, he has been a stabilizing force in a wide receiver room that once again played without D.J. Moore. Coleman caught four of his six targets for 59 yards and a TD and also drew a clutch pass interference penalty. Defensively, cornerback Christian Benford excelled in coverage against Brock Bowers (four catches for 70 yards but no targets in the first half); linebacker Dorian Williams provided a huge lift with his first career interception; defensive tackle Deone Walker continued to excel as a run stuffer; and rookie cornerback Davison Igbinosun had the best game of his young career, finishing with three pass breakups. But the negatives on defense were hard to ignore, as Buffalo allowed Las Vegas to score on six of its 10 drives, averaging 6.2 yards per play, including 7.32 yards/play on scoring drives. The Raiders posted 14 plays that went for 10+ yards, including nine plays of 15+ yards. The Raiders converted on 7 of 12 third-down opportunities (58.3%), and the middle of the field was wide open for Kirk Cousins (23 of 41 for 313 yards, two TDs and an INT) to locate Tre Tucker (five catches for 97 yards and two TDs), Michael Mayer (seven catches for 95 yards), and Bowers downfield. Coleman caught four of his six targets for 59 yards and a TD and also drew a clutch pass interference penalty. Defensively, cornerback Christian Benford excelled in coverage against Brock Bowers (four catches for 70 yards but no targets in the first half); linebacker Dorian Williams provided a huge lift with his first career interception; defensive tackle Deone Walker continued to excel as a run stuffer; and rookie cornerback Davison Igbinosun had the best game of his young career, finishing with three pass breakups. But the negatives on defense were hard to ignore, as Buffalo allowed Las Vegas to score on six of its 10 drives, averaging 6.2 yards per play, including 7.32 yards/play on scoring drives. The Raiders posted 14 plays that went for 10+ yards, including nine plays of 15+ yards. The Raiders converted on 7 of 12 third-down opportunities (58.3%), and the middle of the field was wide open for Kirk Cousins (23 of 41 for 313 yards, two TDs and an INT) to locate Tre Tucker (five catches for 97 yards and two TDs), Michael Mayer (seven catches for 95 yards), and Bowers downfield. item.title: At Strasbourg, Gio Reyna is starting to gain what had been elusive: momentum
item.description: A goal against PSG is proof on the scoresheet of what can be seen on the teamsheet: at long last, Reyna is getting consistent minutes For an entire four-year cycle, to write about Gio Reyna was to write about his potential – especially the nagging feeling that it was going unfulfilled. Once hyped as possibly the greatest prospect in US men’s history, a series of injuries kept him from simply taking the field, much less making his mark on it. Since his emergent 2020-21 season, when he logged nearly 2,000 Bundesliga minutes running alongside Erling Haaland, Jude Bellingham, and Jadon Sancho, Reyna finished each of the ensuing five seasons without even cresting 630 league minutes. “Rotational” became a generous descriptor for his role at Nottingham Forest on loan, and then last season with Borussia Mönchengladbach. Still, Gregg Berhalter and Mauricio Pochettino kept involving Reyna with the US squad based on that pesky potential – betting that, on his day, he still had the raw talent to do what few compatriots could. item.title: Another unremarkable win shows Arsenal’s strength is in depth rather than creativity | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: Champions so risk-averse Forest were lured into thinking they had a chance, until bench was used to see them off Pass. Pass. Pass. Pass. Sideways. Square. Backwards. Pass. Pass. Recycle. Pass. It wasn’t much of a spectacle. But in the end, for the second week running, thanks in no small part of their bench, Arsenal won. Fireworks in the autumn are for Bonfire Night; titles require relentless accumulation. Since the international break, Arsenal have won three games out of three despite not being in the lead at half-time in any of them. Hammered at Brighton and having endured a drab first hour at home to Leeds last week, there has been a rare sense, for the first time really since Manchester City dropped points at Everton at the beginning of May, of Arsenal not being quite at their best, needing to reassert their quality. This was not a performance that would terrify any opponent, but it did highlight Arsenal’s consistency and it did demonstrate just how deep their squad now runs. Continue reading...

item.title: Europe is a blast – but more a curse than a blessing if you are not a Premier League super-club I Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.title: Houthi conflict casts shadow as Saudi Arabia scales back sporting pipe dreams
item.description: A match delayed by missile attack warnings is not what Cristiano Ronaldo and co signed up for but it’s the new reality; the Saudi sporting juggernaut is stalling Cristiano Ronaldo grabbed the scarf in the colours of the Saudi Arabian flag and waved it at the sparse but enthusiastic crowd, who responded with rapturous cheers. It was a gesture of defiance rather than a victory salute, encapsulating the Saudi equivalent of “Keep calm and carry on”. Monday night’s Asian Champions League Elite game between Al-Nassr and the Uzbek side Neftchi Fergana had ended with a 3-1 win for the Saudi club coached by Ange Postecoglou, with Ronaldo, supported by Sadio Mané, scoring, the smattering of star names indicative of the lure of the Saudi Pro League. Yet this isn’t quite how Ronaldo and co would have anticipated life in Riyadh. The meagre attendance aside, Monday’s game was delayed by a threat of missile attacks from Yemen’s Houthi rebels. A safety warning issued 15 minutes before kick-off came two days after 13 people died and more than 300 were wounded by Houthi strikes on Riyadh’s King Khalid international airport. item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! It is quite funny that PSG felt like the good guys at the Etihad Stadium but if we briefly detach ourselves from the notion that the European champions’ own sportswashing and cashsplashing has also done immeasurable damage to the beautiful game, then their 4-2 Bigger Cup shellacking of Manchester City was pure cinema, baby! I was stunned at reading the comments in support of Manchester City keeping their trophies, coming out of the mouth of their Bigger Cup rivals at PSG (yesterday’s Quote of the Day). Given the example of the organisers of the Tour de Lance … sorry, the Tour de France, this kind of ‘keep the awards you won’ stuff might get him sent to the Bastille. Or consider Formula One. They’ve got all kinds of rules about driver behaviour on the racetrack, and additional rules about what the crew can and cannot do to your car. Cars get inspected before each race, and there are also mandatory post-race inspections for every car. You might drive your car first across the line to the cheers of the crowd, but if the post-race inspection discovered that you cheated in how your team designed your vehicle, your memory of crossing the line is all you get to keep. Think about that for a minute. If the Premier League and Fifa cannot clear the bar for morals in sport set by the UCI and FIA, that says a lot. And none of it good” – Peter Rehwaldt. My friend Bernard grew up in Coventry. And as a boy he thought the team was called ‘Coventry City Nil’. I would get out more, but I’m a Manchester United fan” – Brendan Hughes. It is all about maintaining an independent football association and the trappings and privilege that come with it. There was some talk a few years ago about getting a Hong Kong team in the Chinese Super League, when the spending was in full flow, and although that did not happen the local Premier League has belatedly got in on the act – kind of. This glittering city is not known as a football hotbed but has a long history in the sport that started when it was a British colony and has continued since it became a special administrative region of China in 1997. George Best, Peter Shilton, Arie Haan, Bobby Moore, Diego Forlán, Nicky Butt, René van de Kerkhof, Tony Morley, Gordon McQueen and Craig Foster have played in the territory and soon David Silva will too. item.description: The winger is 28, and younger teammates are rising into the high-pressure spots he has usually occupied Usually, the second weekend of October sees Christian Pulisic flanked by compatriots as the Star-Spangled Banner plays. item.description: It’s not just that the club’s recent charges themselves are unprecedented – it’s the language used to describe them too Sign up for our free newsletter here The language of football is a fine and highly nuanced dialect. The majority of people involved in the game speak it with a high degree of sophistication. Minor deviations from the familiar, almost imperceptible to outsiders, can set off alarm bells: what’s really going on there? Why isn’t he happy? What’s she hinting at? But it’s an argot developed to talk about football, and when applied to other subjects, it can sound extremely jarring. Erling Haaland is one of the brighter, more engaging players. There’s an appealing quirkiness to him that suggests he has a higher-than-usual level of self-awareness. He doesn’t mind stepping outside the norms, being a bit different. item.title: Why we’re stuck with a Premier League in the clutches of the global mega-rich | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: There’s little prospect of the model changing in a country that welcomes wealthy international owners with open arms Football, the world’s most popular sport, played by laws drawn up in London in 1863. The Premier League is the UK’s greatest soft power export. Premier League clubs are owned by a deputy prime minister of Abu Dhabi, the public investment fund of Saudi Arabia, a billionaire based in Monaco for tax reasons and a disappointing assortment of investors and private equity funds. And what, really, could be more British than that? Football truly is the national game. What the Manchester City case has exposed is just how difficult it is to regulate some of the richest and most powerful bodies in the world. While the wait for the verdict was frustrating, it was perhaps unavoidable given the possibility of legal objection at every turn when a leaked email from City’s in-house lawyer during Uefa’s action against the club had threatened to “ spend 30 million on the 50 best lawyers in the world to sue them for the next 10 years”. item.content:encoded: There’s little prospect of the model changing in a country that welcomes wealthy international owners with open arms Football, the world’s most popular sport, played by laws drawn up in London in 1863. The Premier League is the UK’s greatest soft power export. Premier League clubs are owned by a deputy prime minister of Abu Dhabi, the public investment fund of Saudi Arabia, a billionaire based in Monaco for tax reasons and a disappointing assortment of investors and private equity funds. And what, really, could be more British than that? Football truly is the national game. What the Manchester City case has exposed is just how difficult it is to regulate some of the richest and most powerful bodies in the world. While the wait for the verdict was frustrating, it was perhaps unavoidable given the possibility of legal objection at every turn when a leaked email from City’s in-house lawyer during Uefa’s action against the club had threatened to “ spend 30 million on the 50 best lawyers in the world to sue them for the next 10 years”. You didn’t get that with Albert Alexander Sr or Peter Swales. Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17.
